evaluator: Fictionalized Margaret Morse analytical lens (independent advisory simulation; no participation, quotation, endorsement, review, or hiring decision by Margaret Morse)
evidence: The homepage provides a one-click path to About, where “Systems people can inhabit” explicitly connects artistic, civic, technical, and social practice while retaining a clear technical-project-management and implementation frame.

The About page establishes more than three public-safe continuities: Open House connects communal governance and many-perspective documentation to WOWList’s organizer-shaped publishing, Sunday Dinner/196’s hospitality and participation infrastructure, NYC Artist Coalition/FairRentNYC’s collective civic memory, and source-backed team memory’s correctable handoffs.

The portfolio explains the distinguishing operating principle directly: systems should let people recognize relationships, participate, remember what happened, influence or correct the record, and continue the work; requirements, interfaces, documentation, and handoffs matter because people must inhabit them.

The project traces are concrete rather than merely thematic: WOWList follows community language instead of a central editorial taxonomy; Sunday Dinner/196 integrates invitations, hosting, onboarding, access, documentation, and continuity; coalition work links testimony, meetings, public sources, decisions, question logs, and action trackers.

The public resume preserves professional legibility through quantified and role-relevant evidence—14+ years, 2x revenue growth, 30+ pages of campaign memory, 35 city ecosystems, 300+ gatherings, and 20+ resident artists—without converting the portfolio into an artist biography.

The supplied desktop and mobile screenshots show the About lineage rendered within one click of the homepage and demonstrate that the material remains available responsively; the Colophon visibly states the edition’s review, credit, permission, and source-custody rules.
gaps: The mobile About page is text-dense, so the strongest continuity evidence requires substantial scrolling even though it remains within the required one-click route.

Open House functions mainly as the historical threshold; its evidentiary grounding depends on the bounded public-source note rather than a fuller on-page case study. This is appropriately cautious but leaves that lineage less inspectable than the current-project traces.
safety_findings: The packet explicitly excludes UCSC narrative evaluations, grades, student identifiers, private correspondence, and unapproved testimonial language; none is quoted or projected in the reviewed rendered text.
Open House is described with bounded first-person initiation while communal decision-making and documentation remain attributed to participants, avoiding sole-authorship inflation.
Collective projects consistently use shared-credit language, including “co-founded,” “co-built,” “helped,” “collaborators,” and statements that outcomes remain collective.
Sunday Dinner/196 explicitly keeps private participant records private and rejects turning community records into public spectacle.

The Colophon separates evidentiary support from permission to publish, treats named page-owner perspectives as fictionalized simulations, and denies them authority to grant consent, settle facts, assign credit, or publish.

Photographic and archival material is presented with project-specific credits and bounded reuse language; the manifest expressly states that portfolio authorization does not establish depicted-person endorsement or broader reuse.
recommendation: Pass PR-015. Preserve the concise About-page threshold and its explicit professional framing; future refinement should improve mobile scanability without adding protected records, private praise, or stronger authorship claims.
